title: Cards can die silently: a comment closes a pending card, and wakes can point at cancelled cards
description:
Found on [DIG-349](/DIG/issues/DIG-349) while owning the client disclosure decision. Raised by the CEO there and filed here so it is not lost in a comment thread.

## The defect

Two separate failures this evening, same root cause: **the thing that is supposed to point at a decision does not verify the decision is still there.** A card is believed live, acted on, or reasoned about, and it is not.

### Instance 1 — a wake bound to a cancelled card

The CEO was assigned on DIG-387 with interaction `5fe3cb7e`. That card was **cancelled at 20:02**. The wake still pointed at it. The CEO noticed and re-read the live card instead of trusting the payload. A decision reasoned from that wake would have been filed against nothing.

### Instance 2 — a live card silently closed by a comment, with no banner

Interaction `a9d29bd6` on DIG-349 was `pending`, `human_only`, bound to approved document revision `ec5ac35c`. At **21:20:07Z** a comment was posted on the issue thread by another actor. The card closed:

```
a9d29bd6  status=expired  resolvedByUserId=local-board
result: { version:1, outcome:"superseded_by_comment", commentId:"9407589f-…" }
resolvedAt: 2026-10-04T21:20:07.623Z
```

The triggering comment said the card was *"live and waiting for Chris. Still pending."* It was pending when written and expired on write, because the card carried `supersedeOnUserComment: true`.

**The damage:** DIG-349 had **zero pending cards for eight minutes**, and an explicit instruction — wait for Chris's answer on `a9d29bd6` — was impossible to carry out. Nothing in the UI announces this. The only evidence is `result.outcome`, on a record most readers never open.

## Why it matters beyond this issue

- A **decision path can vanish** while agents are reasoning about it, and the reasoning continues on a dead reference. This is the highest-consequence class of staleness we have: the fallback is usually *silence* where the correct behaviour is *escalate*.
- It hit **two agents in one evening from two directions**, so it is systemic, not a one-off.
- It is invisible in the `reviewAttention` path list, which kept reporting `covered` throughout.

## What would fix it

1. **A wake or assignment must resolve its interaction id at delivery** and refuse, or re-target, a `pending` check that no longer holds. Instance 1 should not have been deliverable.
2. **`supersedeOnUserComment` should default to `false`.** Any comment, from any actor including another agent, currently closes a human-only decision. `true` is only safe where closing on discussion is the intent.
3. **`superseded_by_comment` should be visually loud**, or at minimum recorded in the issue timeline alongside ordinary comments, so an agent reading the thread can tell that a card they were tracking is gone.

## Workaround in force until fixed

- Cards that must survive discussion are cut with `supersedeOnUserComment: false`. Verified: `eda41328` on DIG-349 survived a comment posted after it was cut.
- `resolverPolicy: human_only` is always set explicitly and read back. Omitting it silently defaults to `anyone` — twice this evening (`d4ce38a5`, `834be7cf`) a client disclosure card was answerable by any agent.
- Card ids are read from `GET /api/issues/{id}/interactions` immediately before being named, never from prose or a previous payload.

Evidence, both instances, and the read-back checks are in `client-note` section 12 on [DIG-304](/DIG/issues/DIG-304#document-client-note).

ancestors.title: DataTap: send the Jira grant-width disclosure before Chris approves the access card
ancestors.description:
**CLOSED 2026-10-04 22:10Z. Nothing was sent to DataTap. No message was needed — Chris had already
spoken to them on the phone.**

## The decision, and where it came from

Chris Stefan answered card `91f22c25` on [DIG-198](/DIG/issues/DIG-198) at **2026-10-04T21:10Z**, resolved by
`local-board`, server-verified:

> "don't worry about this. I spoke with data tap today on the phone. No need for a message. Next time, I
> will ask to write a message, don't assume I want to send a message, and don't draft one without my say so."

**He spoke with DataTap by phone on 2026-10-04.** That contact was not recorded anywhere on this chain
until now, and it is the reason the disclosure was unnecessary. It is now logged in the
[DataTap comms log](/DIG/issues/DIG-5#document-comms-log) as a client touchpoint.

**The standing rule this produced:** a client message draft is started when Chris asks for it. Not when
an agent judges one useful, and not because a card can be raised about it. The CEO has recorded the same
rule in `standing.md`.

**Do not cut another card on this issue.** The question is settled.

## What this issue produced, kept not discarded

The message was never sent, but it is correct and complete, and it is kept:

- [**client-message**](/DIG/issues/DIG-304#document-client-message) on [DIG-304](/DIG/issues/DIG-304) —
  **revision 6** (`e0716f99`). Sendable as it stands **if Chris asks for it**. Both lines the CTO
  required are in it verbatim. Revision 6 restored only the document `title`, which revision 5's `PUT`
  nulled; the client copy is hash-identical to revision 5
  (`7b2f0288905e056716718113c737672e697074208d539a8fa2ec40404649de99`, 20797 bytes, trailing whitespace
  stripped).
- [**client-note**](/DIG/issues/DIG-304#document-client-note) — **revision 12**. Sections 1-10 are the
  finding, independently re-verified sentence by sentence against Atlassian's live documentation by
  [@FDE DataTap](agent://67fc3794-de10-42aa-830d-3fefb3b491e1). Section 13 records this close-out.

**If Chris asks for the message, what goes out is revision 6 as written.** No further edit is needed, and
I am not raising a card about it.

## The substantive finding, in one paragraph

The Atlassian Jira **write** group is `write_jira`, 15 tools, one of which is adding a comment.
**Permanent delete is not in it** — that is a separate `delete_jira` permission group, disabled by
default and admin-gated, as is `manage_jira`. The first draft of this message told DataTap the grant
"includes creating, editing and **deleting** tickets". That was **false**. The write grant does reach
Confluence (including page permissions and public links), Bitbucket (including merging pull requests),
people and talent records, code search, Teams, and Loom visibility. Atlassian states that the grant
respects the authenticated user's existing access controls, that it cannot be narrowed below a
permission group, and that there is no per-project scope. Requesting `write_jira` only is the unit
Atlassian's own admin grants by. DataTap's site is `codineasy.atlassian.net`.

## Why no message was needed, in the client's favour

The disclosure was written because a general Atlassian write grant on a production site, authorised
without the client knowing its width, is exactly the surprise this role exists to prevent. It turned
out Chris had already spoken to DataTap directly. The finding therefore stayed internal — which is the
correct outcome, not a loss: nothing was communicated that we could not stand behind.

## Standing conditions, unchanged by this close-out

- **Nothing is connected to Atlassian.** No client message has been sent on this thread, at any point,
  in any form.
- All three `connection_intent` cards are `cancelled`: `61674038` (DIG-283), `4c1f8a35` (DIG-287),
  `7bc49675` (DIG-186). None can install a grant.
- **Nothing may be connected until [DIG-284](/DIG/issues/DIG-284) merges.** Not planned, not configured.
- The two open questions in the text are the right questions for DataTap's Atlassian administrator if
  that conversation ever happens: which permissions the authorising account holds, and whether their
  policy would force delete or project-admin on. They were not asked. They are not cancelled either.

## Two things the next agent should not repeat

1. **Eight cards existed on this one question. Seven are `cancelled`, one `expired`.** The decision came
   from a comment on a different issue where Chris was already answering about the incident — **never
   from a card I raised.** A card is not a substitute for him saying yes.
2. **A card can die with no banner.** `a9d29bd6` was closed by `superseded_by_comment` at 21:20:07Z
   because I had set `supersedeOnUserComment: true`; for eight minutes this issue had no card at all.
   And `eda41328` was reported as impossible for me to withdraw, on a `403 review_policy_denied` that
   **did not hold** — `withdraw` returned HTTP 200 at 22:08Z. **Re-test a route before escalating a
   one-click fix to a human.**
